newsitem.title: BELGIUM: D'IETEREN MARKET SHARE CONTINUES TO RISE.
newsitem.headline: D'IETEREN MARKET SHARE CONTINUES TO RISE.

text.p: Belgian car importer and distributer D'Ieteren said on Thursday its market share edged further up to 19.81 percent in 1996 from 19.58 percent the previous year.
"We had a very good automobile market," Thierry van Kan, general director of D'Ieteren Auto, told a news conference.
He said D'Ieteren sold 85,168 cars in 1996, up 12.1 percent against 1995. This compared with a total of 397,359 new cars for Belgium, up 10.7 percent on 1995.

Cars distributed by D'Ieteren, which imports Volkswagen (VW), Audi, Porsche , Seat and Skoda brands, totalled 755,377 at the end of 1996 against 730,481 in 1995. Belgium has a total car park of 4.31 million.
Van Kan said he expected sales to nudge further up in 1997.
"We think that a market of 400,000 cars is in the pipeline," he said. "A market share of 20 percent is a realistic target."
He dismissed a drop in sales in January as non-significant.
"A trainload of cars blocked for two days, and it's already 10 percent lower," he said. "We've already recouped a considerable part of that drop in February," he said.
He said that sales of new cars would be fanned by consumer demand for cars with lower fuel consumption and higher safety.
D'Ieteren will also profit from the launch later this year of the new Golf, Audi A6 and Porsche 996 models, he said.
